tagline: A stone mill and a crossroads post frame the county’s road stories.
intro: Millwood’s stone gristmill, White Post’s crossroads and the road to Paris Mountain give this county drive its anchors. Blue Ridge Mountain Road reaches Paris Mountain from Ashby Gap, above the Shenandoah Valley. Virginia Byways are state-designated scenic roads intended to introduce travelers to alternative destinations.

At Millwood, Nathaniel Burwell financed a mill whose construction Daniel Morgan managed about 1785. The mill worked until the 1950s, then passed to the Clarke County Historical Association in 1964. The association completed restoration in 1970 and operates it as a museum.

Millwood lies southeast of Boyce, where the railway crossed the Winchester and Berry’s Ferry Turnpike. Paris stands at the eastern base of Ashby Gap, and Blue Ridge Mountain Road provides the mountain connection from the gap. White Post centers on White Post Road and Berrys Ferry Road; Greenway Court lies south of the village, down a private drive.

moments.title: Burwell-Morgan Mill
moments.text: A stone in the mill wall carries the overseer’s initials and the date 1782. The mill’s construction is dated about 1785, with Nathaniel Burwell financing the project and Daniel Morgan managing it. The gable-roofed building measures approximately 45 by 60 feet. Stone lower levels support a frame upper story and attic added around 1876. After milling ended in the 1950s, restoration made the building a museum. Its water wheel is a rebuilt one made of Peruvian mahogany. The Clarke County Historical Association received it in 1964 and completed its restoration six years later, in 1970.
moments.notice: The mill wall bears L.H. Mongrul’s initials and the date 1782.

moments.title: Blue Ridge Mountain Road
moments.text: Blue Ridge Mountain Road gives access to Paris Mountain from Ashby Gap. Paris Mountain rises to 1,926 feet just north of the gap. Its summit is the highest point in both Clarke and Loudoun counties. The Appalachian Trail crosses the peak’s western slope. SR 601, also called Blue Ridge Mountain Road, is the approach to the Mount Weather Emergency Operations Center. The site began as a weather station in the late 1800s; its research observatory operated from 1904 to 1914. An underground facility was completed in 1959, and FEMA established surface training facilities in 1979.

moments.title: White Post
moments.text: The bronze plaque on White Post’s marker records a tradition: George Washington placed the original post to direct travelers to Lord Fairfax’s residence. Fairfax employed the young Washington as a surveyor on his extensive landholdings. His seat, Greenway Court, lies south of the village. The original house was pulled down after its roof collapsed in 1834. The surviving land office is a limestone building from about 1762. The crossroads itself joins White Post Road and Berrys Ferry Road off US 340. Greenway Court’s private drive lies on White Post Road, south of the village.
